Install

You need Claude Code 1.0.33 or newer. Run these three commands inside it:

/plugin marketplace add AgriciDaniel/claude-seo
/plugin install claude-seo@agricidaniel-claude-seo
/seo setup

/seo setup prepares everything Claude SEO needs (its own Python environment and a headless browser) without touching the rest of your system. Run /seo doctor any time to check it.

Manual install: macOS and Linux 
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/AgriciDaniel/claude-seo.git
bash claude-seo/install.sh

One-liner (curl, review then run):

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AgriciDaniel/claude-seo/main/install.sh > install.sh
cat install.sh        # review before running
bash install.sh
rm install.sh
Manual install: Windows (PowerShell) 
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/AgriciDaniel/claude-seo.git
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File claude-seo\install.ps1

Why git clone instead of irm | iex? Claude Code's own security guardrails flag irm ... | iex as a supply chain risk: downloading and executing remote code without verification. The git clone approach lets you inspect claude-seo\install.ps1 before running it.

Two versions. This public version is MIT licensed and free for everyone. AI Marketing Hub Pro members also get a private version with early access to new features. Members install it with:

/plugin marketplace add AI-Marketing-Hub/claude-seo
/plugin install claude-seo@ai-marketing-hub-claude-seo
/seo setup

Your first audit:

claude                                   # start Claude Code

/seo audit https://example.com           # full site audit with a prioritized plan
/seo page https://example.com/pricing    # one page, in depth
/seo geo https://example.com             # how ready you are for AI search
/seo schema https://example.com          # check and generate structured data
/seo local https://example.com           # local SEO and Google Business Profile

FAQ

What is Claude SEO?

A free, open-source SEO audit tool that runs inside Claude Code. It checks technical SEO, Core Web Vitals, content quality, Schema.org structured data, AI search readiness, local SEO, e-commerce and international SEO, then gives you a prioritized action plan. It follows Google's own documentation, including the AI Optimization Guide.

Is it really free?

Yes. It is MIT licensed, with no per-site pricing, no usage limits and no tracking. You only need Claude Code. A few optional extensions connect to paid services where you bring your own account, but everything works without them.

Do I need API keys?

No. Claude SEO works out of the box. If you want real field data, you can connect free Google APIs (PageSpeed Insights, Chrome UX Report, Search Console and Google Analytics 4) with /seo google setup. Your keys stay on your machine.

How does it help with AI search like Google AI Overviews and ChatGPT?

Google says optimizing for AI search is still SEO, so Claude SEO starts with the basics that AI answers rely on: being indexed, fast and clear. Then /seo geo scores how easy your pages are to quote, checks that AI crawlers can reach them and looks at your brand's presence on Wikipedia, Reddit, YouTube and LinkedIn. /seo agentic checks how well AI agents can use your site.

Does it work on JavaScript sites like Next.js, React or Vue?

Yes. When a page needs JavaScript to show its content, Claude SEO opens it in a headless browser automatically, so single-page apps are audited as visitors see them.

How is it different from Screaming Frog or other SEO tools?

Crawlers like Screaming Frog crawl faster and deeper, and big SEO suites have their own backlink databases. Claude SEO does something else: it explains what it finds, sorts it by impact, covers AI search in depth and lets you ask follow-up questions in plain English. Many people use both.

Does my data leave my computer?

Claude SEO runs inside Claude Code, so the pages and data it analyzes are sent to Claude, Anthropic's model, the same as anything else you work on in Claude Code. Reports are saved as files on your machine. No SEO service or other third party sees your data unless you connect an extension or API yourself. Besides the site you audit, some checks read public sources such as Wikipedia, Reddit and Common Crawl. See PRIVACY.md for the full list.

Good to know: requirements, limits and uninstall

Requirements. Claude Code 1.0.33 or newer and Python 3.11 to 3.14. /seo setup installs the headless browser for you.

Cost of a full audit. Five agents that need more judgment run on Opus and the rest on Sonnet, so a full /seo audit uses more of your Claude plan than a single-page check. You can change any agent's model in its file under agents/.

Limits. Without Google API keys, Core Web Vitals are lab estimates and indexing is inferred from the page. Pages that load key content only after scrolling or clicking can give noisy results.

Uninstall. Installed as a plugin: /plugin uninstall claude-seo@agricidaniel-claude-seo. Installed manually:

git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/AgriciDaniel/claude-seo.git
bash claude-seo/uninstall.sh

Extensions

Optional add-ons that bring in more data. Claude SEO works fully without them.

  • Banana: AI images for SEO, from social previews to blog heroes (Claude Banana)
  • SE Ranking: your share of voice in ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google AI answers
  • Profound: tracks when AI models cite your site
  • Bing Webmaster: Bing data plus instant IndexNow submission
  • Unlighthouse: Lighthouse scores for every page of your site

Setup guides live in extensions/.

Integrations built and maintained by other people, in their own repositories, are listed in Community integrations. They are not part of Claude SEO and are not audited by it.

releases.name: v2.6.0: deterministic page, TLS, sitemap and JavaScript-gap checks
releases.body:
Deterministic checks ported from web-obs, the sister crawler project. Work
that the skills asked the model to do by hand (count sitemap URLs, compare
served and rendered HTML, read a certificate, check a page's basics) is now
done by scripts with tests. Two new scripts, 63 in total.

**After updating, run `/seo setup` once** (one new dependency, PySocks).

**Drift baselines:** a page whose JSON-LD script tag is typed in upper case or
with a parameter (`application/ld+json; charset=utf-8`) was skipped before and
is read now, so it shows one schema change. Re-baseline after updating.

### Added

- **`page_checks.py`: 47 on-page checks in one script.** Title, description,
  headings, canonical, robots, hreflang, document basics, images, links, URL
  hygiene, size, Open Graph, JSON-LD validity and thin content. Each finding
  has a stable id, a severity, a message and trimmed evidence. Length
  thresholds follow `quality-gates.md` and are worded as display heuristics,
  not Google rules. `/seo page` runs it first.
- **`transport_check.py`: TLS certificate, security headers and redirects.**
  Certificate validity, days to expiry, host and www coverage and trust;
  grades for HSTS, CSP

releases.name: v2.5.1: 45 community fixes, urllib3 security floor
releases.body:
Community fixes: 39 pull requests from 18 contributors, 6 dependency updates, and the follow-up fixes found while reviewing them. No new commands. **After updating, run `/seo setup` once.** The dependency floors changed (urllib3 2.8.0 fixes three advisories), so the managed runtime rebuilds. **Drift baselines:** three parser fixes change stored values once. A page with a JSON-LD `@graph` shows one `schema_modified` warning, and a heading that holds an inline tag or a `
` shows one heading change. Re-baseline after updating. ### Security - **urllib3 floor raised to 2.8.0** (#323). It fixes GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77 (HTTPS proxy TLS settings ignored), GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw (unbounded chunk-size buffering) and GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g (chunked deflate loop). - **A `host:port` entry in `CLAUDE_SEO_LOCAL_TARGETS` now holds for the whole request.** The DNS pin on a non-public address answered for every port, so a redirect from the allowed dev server could reach another service on that host. It now answers only for the validated port, or another port the allowlist names. Public hosts are unchanged. The port-bound pin was first proposed by @joachimBrindeau in #318. - **Google prop

releases.name: v2.5.0: Python 3.11+, security and accuracy fixes, Claude Desktop installs
releases.body:
Security and accuracy fixes from a full audit, and Claude Desktop installs again.

**Python 3.11 to 3.14 is now required.** Python 3.10 reached end of life on
2026-10-01, and the Pillow 13.0.0 security release (28 advisories, no 12.x
backport) needs 3.11. Python 3.15 is not supported yet because the Google Ads
client library declares `< 3.15`. If your default Python is outside the range,
the launcher and `install.ps1` now pick a supported one on their own, or you
can set `CLAUDE_SEO_PYTHON`; `/seo setup` then rebuilds the runtime once.

### Install or update

```
/plugin marketplace add AgriciDaniel/claude-seo
/plugin install claude-seo@agricidaniel-claude-seo
/plugin install seo-cockpit@agricidaniel-claude-seo   # optional, needs Claude Code 2.1.287+
```

Already installed? `claude plugin update claude-seo@agricidaniel-claude-seo` (auto-update is off by default for third-party marketplaces). If you use seo-cockpit, update it too: it now installs from its own branch, which is what lets Claude Desktop load claude-seo again (#344).

### Added

- **Server stack CVE exposure check** in `seo-technical` (Security category).
  A read-only detection pass that flags a site running a server

releases.name: v2.4.1: Google-currency patch (September 2026 spam update)
releases.body:
Claude SEO v2.4.1 is a patch release that brings Google guidance current through 2026-09-28, including the September 2026 spam update (started 2026-09-24 and still rolling out when this release was cut; Google named no target). Every changed fact was re-checked against its primary source, and claims that could not be confirmed on a Google-owned page, such as the SAFE detector or "link spam is excluded", are recorded as unverified so audits never state them as fact. The release went through two independent reviews, a clean-room verification run with live headless `/seo` sessions, and green CI on Linux, macOS and Windows (including PowerShell 5.1).


### Added

- Ledger (`data/google-updates.json`): the September 2026 Spam Update
  (started 2026-09-24, still rolling out when this release was cut; Google
  estimates up to two weeks and named no target), the August 2025 Spam
  Update, VideoObject `creator` and the `interactionStatistic` action types,
  Search Console multimodal reporting, Merchant Center AI performance
  insights, the UCP integration hub cart transfer, Gemini 3.8 Flash in AI
  Mode for subscribers, and CrUX experimental ad metrics.
- `unverified[]` entries so audits do

aiSummary.oneLiner: Free open-source SEO audits and action plans powered directly within Claude Code.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Claude SEO is an advanced, open-source SEO skill built specifically for Claude Code. It executes complete website SEO audits in minutes using 26 sub-skills and 19 specialized AI agents running in parallel. It analyzes technical SEO, E-E-A-T, schema markup, AI search compatibility, and local/e-commerce SEO factors. The audits yield actionable recommendations directly within the developer's workflow.
keyFeatures: Parallel agent auditing: deploys up to 17 specialized AI agents concurrently for comprehensive site analysis.
Comprehensive checks: analyzes technical SEO, Core Web Vitals, E-E-A-T, and structured data.
AI search optimization: evaluates your site's visibility for Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini.
Drift monitoring: monitors SEO changes over time using SQLite snapshots to catch regressions between audits.
Actionable plans: provides specific recommendations detailing why it matters and how to verify the fix.
